lem-du-activation-normalizer-finite-posi:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $Z$ have the standard normal law on $\mathbb R$. Suppose $\sigma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is analytic, nonpolynomial, satisfies $|\sigma(0)|\le B$ for some finite $B$, and is $L$-Lipschitz for a finite $L$. Then $0<\mathbb E[\sigma(Z)^2]<\infty$. Consequently the normalization constant

$$c_\sigma:=\bigl(\mathbb E[\sigma(Z)^2]\bigr)^{-1}$$

is a well-defined positive finite real number.
lem-du-conditional-loss-contraction-unde:
## Statement

Let $r\in\mathbb R^n$, let $G$ be a real symmetric matrix with eigenvalues in $[\lambda,\Lambda]$ for some $0<\lambda\le\Lambda$, and suppose $0<\eta\Lambda\le1$. If an update has the form $r^+=(I-\eta G)r+R$ with $\|R\|_2\le\eta\lambda\|r\|_2/4$, then for the quadratic loss $L=\frac12\|r\|_2^2$ and $L^+=\frac12\|r^+\|_2^2$,

$$L^+\le(1-\eta\lambda/2)L.$$
def-du-overparameterized-network-archite:
## Definition

Assume AC, DC and countable choice for the Gaussian probability-law constructions below. The displayed finite real network recurrences and empirical loss are deterministic definitions for fixed parameters. Fix positive integers $d,n,H,m$, training inputs $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d$ with $\|x_i\|_2=1$, labels $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb R$, an analytic nonpolynomial activation $\sigma$ satisfying $|\sigma(0)|<\infty$ and finite Lipschitz constants for $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$, and the positive finite normalization $c_\sigma=(\mathbb E_{Z\sim N(0,1)}[\sigma(Z)^2])^{-1}$. A fully connected network of width $m$ and depth $H$ is the finite feedforward recurrence

$$x^{(0)}=x,\qquad x^{(h)}=\sqrt{c_\sigma/m}\,\sigma(W^{(h)}x^{(h-1)})\quad(1\le h\le H),\qquad f_{\rm fc}(x,\theta)=a^Tx^{(H)},$$

where $W^{(1)}\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}$, $W^{(h)}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ for $h\ge2$, $a\in\mathbb R^m$, and $\sigma$ acts coordinatewise. The residual network uses the same first layer and then

$$x^{(1)}=\sqrt{c_\sigma/m}\,\sigma(W^{(1)}x),\qquad x^{(h)}=x^{(h-1)}+\frac{c_{\rm res}}{H\sqrt m}\,\sigma(W^{(h)}x^{(h-1)})\quad(2\le h\le H),\qquad f_{\rm res}(x,\theta)=a^Tx^{(H)},$$

with $0<c_{\rm res}<1$. In either architecture, random initialization means all entries of all matrices $W^{(h)}$ and of $a$ are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables; all these entries are trained by full-batch gradient descent. The empirical quadratic loss is $L(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(f(x_i,\theta)-y_i)^2$.

For the fully connected architecture and the same fixed data, define the population matrices by

$$K_{ij}^{(0)}=\langle x_i,x_j\rangle.$$

For $1\le h<H$, let $(U_{ij}^{(h)},V_{ij}^{(h)})$ be a centered bivariate normal vector with covariance

$$A_{ij}^{(h)}=\begin{pmatrix}K_{ii}^{(h-1)}&K_{ij}^{(h-1)}\\K_{ji}^{(h-1)}&K_{jj}^{(h-1)}\end{pmatrix},$$

and put $K_{ij}^{(h)}=c_\sigma\mathbb E[\sigma(U_{ij}^{(h)})\sigma(V_{ij}^{(h)})]$. For $h=H$, use the same bivariate-normal definition with $A_{ij}^{(H)}$ formed from $K^{(H-1)}$, and set

$$K_{ij}^{(H)}=c_\sigma K_{ij}^{(H-1)}\mathbb E[\sigma'(U_{ij}^{(H)})\sigma'(V_{ij}^{(H)})].$$

When $H=1$, this last formula uses $K^{(0)}$ directly and there are no intermediate activation-covariance matrices. For the fully connected theorem, this terminal matrix is denoted $K_{\rm fc}^{(H)}$.

For the residual architecture with $H\ge2$, use a separate sequence $S^{(h)}$ and mean vector $b^{(h)}$. Set $S^{(0)}=K^{(0)}$. For $G^{(0)}\sim N_n(0,S^{(0)})$, put

$$S_{ij}^{(1)}=c_\sigma\mathbb E[\sigma(G_i^{(0)})\sigma(G_j^{(0)})],\qquad b_i^{(1)}=\sqrt{c_\sigma}\mathbb E[\sigma(G_i^{(0)})].$$

Write $\alpha=c_{\rm res}/H$. For $2\le h<H$, take a fresh centered Gaussian vector $G^{(h-1)}$ with covariance $S^{(h-1)}$, put $\mu_i^{(h-1)}=\mathbb E[\sigma(G_i^{(h-1)})]$, and define

$$S_{ij}^{(h)}=S_{ij}^{(h-1)}+\alpha\bigl(b_i^{(h-1)}\mu_j^{(h-1)}+b_j^{(h-1)}\mu_i^{(h-1)}\bigr)+\alpha^2\mathbb E[\sigma(G_i^{(h-1)})\sigma(G_j^{(h-1)})],\qquad b_i^{(h)}=b_i^{(h-1)}+\alpha\mu_i^{(h-1)}.$$

For $G\sim N_n(0,S^{(H-1)})$, define the residual terminal matrix by

$$K_{{\rm res},ij}^{(H)}=\frac{c_{\rm res}^2}{H^2}S_{ij}^{(H-1)}\mathbb E[\sigma'(G_i)\sigma'(G_j)].$$

The fully connected and residual convergence statements use $K_{\rm fc}^{(H)}$ and $K_{\rm res}^{(H)}$, respectively. At $H=1$, the two architectures coincide; define $K_{\rm res}^{(1)}=K_{\rm fc}^{(1)}$. The residual recursion above is the scalar specialization of the source's general mean/second-moment recursion, equation (16); in particular it includes the mean cross terms. Its terminal Gaussian covariance is $S^{(H-1)}$, as determined by the finite-width last-layer Gram formula (14).

The residual recurrence has one identity contribution from $x^{(h-1)}$ and one nonlinear contribution at every layer $2\le h\le H$; the arrows below depict that convention for one generic layer and do not enter any proof.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth,node distance=1.3cm]
  \node (in) {$x^{(h-1)}$};
  \node[draw,rectangle,right=1.7cm of in] (act) {$\frac{c_{\rm res}}{H\sqrt m}\sigma(W^{(h)}x^{(h-1)})$};
  \node[draw,circle,right=2.0cm of act] (sum) {$+$};
  \node[right=1.2cm of sum] (out) {$x^{(h)}$};
  \draw[->] (in) -- (act);
  \draw[->] (act) -- (sum);
  \draw[->] (in) to[bend right=28] (sum);
  \draw[->] (sum) -- (out);
\end{tikzpicture}
```
lem-du-population-gram-kernels-are-finit:
## Statement

Assume AC, DC and countable choice. Under the hypotheses and notation defining the Du population Gram recursion, every fully connected matrix $K^{(h)}$, every residual feature second-moment matrix $S^{(h)}$, and both terminal matrices are finite, symmetric, and positive semidefinite. The fully connected matrices satisfy $K_{ii}^{(h)}=1$ for $0\le h<H$. For the residual sequence, $S^{(h)}-b^{(h)}(b^{(h)})^T$ is positive semidefinite for $1\le h<H$; its diagonal is not asserted to equal one.
lem-du-output-gradient-gram-update-ident:
## Statement

For any fixed finite real network obeying either architecture recurrence defined on the A page, let $u(\theta)=(f(x_i,\theta))_{i=1}^n\in\mathbb R^n$, let $y=(y_i)_{i=1}^n$, let $J(\theta)\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have row $i$ equal to the gradient of $f(x_i,\theta)$ with respect to the vector of all trainable parameters, and set $G(\theta)=J(\theta)J(\theta)^T$. For the empirical quadratic loss $L(\theta)=\frac12\|u(\theta)-y\|_2^2$, one full-batch gradient-descent step with step size $\eta>0$ satisfies

$$u(\theta^+)=u(\theta)-\eta G(\theta)(u(\theta)-y)+R,$$

where $\theta^+=\theta-\eta J(\theta)^T(u(\theta)-y)$ and $R$ is the first-order Taylor remainder of the differentiable map $u$ at $\theta$ in direction $-\eta J(\theta)^T(u(\theta)-y)$. No size bound on $R$ is asserted here.
lem-du-initial-output-gaussian-concentra:
## Statement

Assume AC, DC and countable choice. Fix hidden-layer feature vectors $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n\in\mathbb R^m$, form the matrix $\Phi\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ with rows $\phi_i^T$, and let the independent output-weight vector $a\sim N_m(0,I_m)$. Put $u=\Phi a$ and $G=\Phi\Phi^T$. Then for every $0<\delta<1$,

$$P\left\{\|u\|_2\le\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(G)}+\|\Phi\|_{\rm op}\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)}\right\}\ge1-\delta,$$

where $\|\Phi\|_{\rm op}=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|\Phi v\|_2$. The probability is conditional on the fixed hidden-layer features and is over $a$ only.
lem-du-local-pl-descent-and-path-length:
## Statement

Let $u:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^2$, $L=\frac12\|u-y\|^2$, and $r_0=u(\theta_0)-y$. On the closed ball $B(\theta_0,R)$ suppose a block $J_*$ of the output Jacobian satisfies $J_*J_*^T\succeq(\lambda/2)I_n$ and $\|\nabla^2L\|\le S$, with $\lambda,S>0$. If $R>2\sqrt2\|r_0\|/\sqrt\lambda$ and $0<\eta\le1/S$, every fixed-step gradient-descent iterate stays in the ball,

$$L(\theta_k)\le(1-\eta\lambda/2)^kL(\theta_0),\qquad\sum_{k\ge0}\|\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k\|\le2\sqrt2\|r_0\|/\sqrt\lambda.$$

The assertion is trivial for $r_0=0$; otherwise the hypotheses imply $0<\eta\lambda/2\le1$.
lem-du-neighborhood-gram-and-hessian-con:
## Statement

Fix finite real parameters obeying either Du architecture recurrence, with all parameters equipped with the Euclidean norm (Frobenius norm on each matrix block). At a fixed initialization assume all hidden feature norms are at most $B_x$, all matrices $W^{(h)}(0)$ with $h\ge2$ have operator norm at most $B_w\sqrt m$, $\|a(0)\|_2\le B_a\sqrt m$, $\|a(0)\|_4\le B_4m^{1/4}$, and all backward feature derivatives $b_{i,h}(0)=\nabla_{x_i^{(h)}}f_i$ have coordinate maxima at most $B_bM$, where $M\ge1$. For fully connected networks allow $B_x,B_b\le A_0^H$ for a fixed $A_0\ge2$, while $B_w,B_a,B_4$ are fixed independent of $H$. There are $A\ge2,C\ge1$ depending only on $A_0$, these fixed bounds and the activation, with the following bounds; write $T=A^H$. In the residual case the constants depend also on fixed $c_{\rm res}$, and every $T$ below is replaced by a fixed $C$ independent of $H$. Uniformly on any parameter ball $\|\theta-\theta_0\|\le D$ with $D/\sqrt m\le c/T$ (fully connected) or $D/\sqrt m\le c$ (residual),

$$\max_{i,h}\|x_i^{(h)}(\theta)-x_i^{(h)}(\theta_0)\|\le TD/\sqrt m,\qquad \|J(\theta)\|_{\rm op}\le T\sqrt n,$$

$$\max_i\|\nabla^2 f_i(\theta)\|_{\rm op}\le \frac{TM(1+D)}{\sqrt m},\qquad \|J_H(\theta)J_H(\theta)^T-J_H(\theta_0)J_H(\theta_0)^T\|_{\rm op}\le\frac{TnD}{\sqrt m}.$$

In the residual last inequality the upper bound is $CnD/(H^2\sqrt m)$ for $H\ge2$. The residual first-layer and output-vector derivatives are bounded without a factor $1/H$. Consequently, if $r_0=u(\theta_0)-y$ and $L=\frac12\|u-y\|^2$, the loss Hessian on the ball satisfies

$$\|\nabla^2L\|_{\rm op}\le Tn+\frac{T\sqrt n\,(\|r_0\|+T\sqrt nD)M(1+D)}{\sqrt m}.$$

The constants in this last bound can again be fixed independent of $H$ for residual networks. For any segment from $\theta$ to $\theta+h$ contained in the ball, its output Taylor remainder satisfies

$$\|u(\theta+h)-u(\theta)-J(\theta)h\|\le \frac{T\sqrt n M(1+D)}{2\sqrt m}\|h\|^2,$$

with $T$ replaced by fixed $C$ in the residual case.
lem-du-simultaneous-initialization-event:
## Statement

Use either of the two architectures, its own terminal population kernel $K$, and independent Gaussian initialization. Assume AC, DC and countable choice and the activation and bounded-label hypotheses of the convergence theorems. Write $\lambda=\lambda_{\min}(K)>0$, $q=1+\log(16/\delta)$ and $M=\sqrt{1+\log(16mnH/\delta)}$. There are constants $A\ge2$ and $C\ge1$, depending only on the fixed activation bounds, its normalizer, the label bound, and, in the residual case, $c_{\rm res}$, with the following property. For the fully connected case put $T=A^H$; if

$$m\ge C\max\{T n^4/\lambda^4,T n/\delta,T n^2\log(16Hn/\delta)/\lambda^2\},$$

then with probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously:

$$\max_{i,h}\|x_i^{(h)}(0)\|\le T,\quad \max_{h\ge2}\|W^{(h)}(0)\|_{\rm op}\le C\sqrt m,\quad \|a(0)\|_2\le C\sqrt m,\quad \|a(0)\|_4\le C m^{1/4},$$

$$\max_{i,h}\|b_{i,h}(0)\|_\infty\le T M,\quad \lambda_{\min}(J_H(0)J_H(0)^T)\ge3\lambda/4,\quad \|u(0)-y\|^2\le Tnq.$$

Here $J_H$ is the Jacobian block of the last hidden-layer matrix, and $b_{i,h}$ is the derivative of the scalar output with respect to the hidden feature vector $x_i^{(h)}$, so $b_{i,H}=a$. In the residual case $H\ge2$, the same conclusions hold with $T$ replaced everywhere in the conclusions by $C$, provided

$$m\ge C\max\{n^4H^6/\lambda^4,n^2/(\lambda^2H^2),n/\delta,n^2\log(16Hn/\delta)/\lambda^2\}.$$

For residual depth one use the fully connected case. Constants may be enlarged, and $A$ may be increased, simultaneously in these conclusions.
thm-wide-network-gradient-descent-reache:
## Statement

Assume AC, DC and countable choice. Fix positive integers $d,n,H,m$, training data $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d$ and labels $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb R$ with $\|x_i\|_2=1$ and $|y_i|\le C_y$ for a fixed finite constant $C_y$. Let the activation satisfy the Lipschitz and smoothness conditions $|\sigma(0)|\le C_\sigma$, $|\sigma(z)-\sigma(z')|\le L|z-z'|$, and $|\sigma'(z)-\sigma'(z')|\le\beta|z-z'|$ for finite constants, and also be analytic and nonpolynomial. Use the fully connected architecture and population matrix $K_{\rm fc}^{(H)}$ defined on this page, initialized with independent standard normal entries in all weight matrices and the output vector, and trained in all layers by full-batch gradient descent on $L(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(f(x_i,\theta)-y_i)^2$. Write $K^{(H)}=K_{\rm fc}^{(H)}$ and put $\lambda_0=\lambda_{\min}(K^{(H)})$ and assume $\lambda_0>0$. For $0<\delta<1$, if the width and fixed step size satisfy

$$m=\Omega\!\left(2^{O(H)}\max\left\{\frac{n^4}{\lambda_0^4},\frac{n}{\delta},\frac{n^2\log(Hn/\delta)}{\lambda_0^2}\right\}\right),\qquad 0<\eta=O\!\left(\frac{\lambda_0}{n^2 2^{O(H)}}\right),$$

then with probability at least $1-\delta$ over initialization, every gradient-descent iterate $k\ge1$ satisfies

$$L(\theta^{(k)})\le\left(1-\frac{\eta\lambda_0}{2}\right)^kL(\theta^{(0)}).$$

The constants hidden in $O$ and $\Omega$ may depend on the fixed activation and label bounds but not on $n,H,m,\delta$; the step-size constant is small enough that $0<\eta\lambda_0/2<1$. In particular, $L(\theta^{(k)})\to0$ geometrically as $k\to\infty$.
thm-residual-network-polynomial-width-tr:
## Statement

Assume AC, DC and countable choice. Fix positive integers $d,n,H,m$, training data $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d$ and labels $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb R$ with $\|x_i\|_2=1$ and $|y_i|\le C_y$ for a fixed finite constant $C_y$. Let the activation satisfy the Lipschitz and smoothness conditions $|\sigma(0)|\le C_\sigma$, $|\sigma(z)-\sigma(z')|\le L|z-z'|$, and $|\sigma'(z)-\sigma'(z')|\le\beta|z-z'|$ for finite constants, and also be analytic and nonpolynomial. Use the residual architecture with fixed $0<c_{\rm res}<1$ and the population matrix $K_{\rm res}^{(H)}$ defined on this page, initialized with independent standard normal entries in all weight matrices and the output vector, and trained in all layers by full-batch gradient descent on $L(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(f_{\rm res}(x_i,\theta)-y_i)^2$. Write $K^{(H)}=K_{\rm res}^{(H)}$ and put $\lambda_0=\lambda_{\min}(K^{(H)})$ and assume $\lambda_0>0$. For $0<\delta<1$, if

$$m=\Omega\!\left(\max\left\{\frac{n^4H^6}{\lambda_0^4},\frac{n^2}{\lambda_0^2H^2},\frac{n}{\delta},\frac{n^2\log(Hn/\delta)}{\lambda_0^2}\right\}\right),\qquad 0<\eta=O\!\left(\frac{\lambda_0H^2}{n^2}\right),$$

then with probability at least $1-\delta$ over initialization, every gradient-descent iterate $k\ge1$ satisfies

$$L(\theta^{(k)})\le\left(1-\frac{\eta\lambda_0}{2}\right)^kL(\theta^{(0)}).$$

The constants hidden in $O$ and $\Omega$ may depend on the fixed activation, label, and residual-scaling bounds but not on $n,H,m,\delta$; the step-size constant is small enough that $0<\eta\lambda_0/2<1$. In particular, $L(\theta^{(k)})\to0$ geometrically as $k\to\infty$.
